messages:
maya: Heads-up — AcmeCorp asked for a per-org routing override so all their traffic goes to the dedicated GPU pool when header X-Org-Tier=enterprise. They want it activated next week. Thoughts?
jon: hmm — do we even have a safe way to do header-based routing that’s per-customer?
priya: We do header matching at the gateway level already, but we don’t currently tie it to an org allowlist/contract flag. That’s the gap.
alex: Key concerns: priority/precedence, audit (who flipped it), and quota counting. If their requests go to dedicated, do we attribute usage to their org or the dedicated pool?
kevin: Attribute to the org — otherwise billing and quota mismatch. Also we must ensure failover to hosted models if dedicated capacity is down.
maya: Agreed on attribution. Also need an admin control in Console + an API to create these overrides. Should be RBAC-protected and show change history.
jon: Proposal: add an "Override" entity with fields: matcher (header/host/path), scope (org_id list), action (route: dedicated|hosted, cache: bypass|normal), priority, enabled, created_by, audit_id.
priya: Love that. For matcher syntax, can we reuse the existing route matcher DSL? e.g.:
```
{
  "matcher": {"type": "header", "name": "X-Org-Tier", "op": "eq", "value": "enterprise"},
  "scope": ["org:acme"],
  "action": {"route": "dedicated-pool-3", "bypass_cache": true},
  "priority": 100
}
```
alex: Need to be careful: header-based matches are easy to spoof unless we validate. For enterprise customers we should require either mTLS or a signed customer assertion header from our edge.
kevin: We already support signed assertions for Private deployments. For hosted customers we can require a signed header issued by our auth service when org is on the allowlist. If not present, matcher should not fire.
maya: UX: In Console, show a banner that this override is active and which orgs are affected. Provide a "test request" modal where SEs can paste headers and we show the route decision and trace id.
jon: Telemetry: tag the request with override_id and route_decision in traces. Add metrics: override_hits, override_misses, override_fallsback. Also a daily report for which overrides increased tail latency or cost.
priya: On quotas — if action routes to dedicated-pool, quota consumption should still decrement the org's quota and also count against reserved capacity metrics. If they exceed org quota, we should return 402 or reroute to hosted fallback depending on policy.
alex: We need a fallback policy field: fallback: {type: "route", target: "hosted-v2", on: ["no_capacity","quota_exceeded"]}. Default is fail-open to hosted.
kevin: Testing plan: create a staging override that matches header X-Test-Override for our test org, run canary at 5% of traffic, and run chaos test where we kill one shard of the dedicated-pool to ensure fallback works.
maya: Security + audit: only ppl in "platform-admins" or "enterprise-eng" can create. Every change writes an immutable audit log entry and emits deploy-bot event.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: override-config updated by maya — id=ovr-20260301-42, canary=5%, target=dedicated-pool-3 :white_check_mark:
jon: One more internal API debate: should overrides live in gateway config (fast path) or in control plane with a cached copy in gateway? If in control plane, need very low-latency cache invalidation.
priya: Control plane with push to gateways seems safer for multi-tenant management and audit. Gateways only read compiled match table for speed. We already push route updates — reuse that path.
alex: Implementation detail: compiled table must include priority order and a flag that forces signature verification. Keep compiled rows small to avoid lookup overhead.
kevin: Ops: add dashboard in Console: list active overrides, hits by org, last fired, last fallback, recent errors. Add alert if overrides cause >1% error increase in the target pool.
maya: Cool. Action items: (1) priya: draft API + DB schema for Override entity, (2) jon: design gateway compiled-table + precedence semantics, (3) kevin: telemetry/billing mapping, (4) alex: threat model + signed header plan. We'll triage in next infra sync.
jon: added to agenda. :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll also draft Console wireframes for the override UI.
priya: I'll drop a PR for the schema tomorrow and include example curl snippets for the admin API.
maya: Thanks — please tag me on the PR. :eyes:
